key_insight: A dual-scale deep learning framework can improve automated detection of mycosis fungoides by combining fine cytological detail from 20x images with broader tissue context from 10x images.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support earlier screening of mycosis fungoides versus benign inflammatory dermatoses and provide a separate clinical-feature model for staging confirmed cases.
method: Late-fusion ensemble of CNNs using paired 10x and 20x histopathology images
Random forest classifier trained on 16 clinical features
Two linked tasks: MF vs non-MF screening and patch/plaque vs tumor staging
evidence_signal: On 6,267 images from 463 patients, the image model reached 83.58% accuracy and 89.13% sensitivity, while the clinical model reached 96.6% accuracy and 93.8% sensitivity.
watch_item: Performance depends on dataset quality and patient-level generalizability, so external validation is needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Detail in Context: A Dual-Scale Machine Learning Framework for Mycosis Fungoides Detection
